Senses.Explanation: (大) great + (死) death / to die: 'the great death.' The corpus glosses the term in its own words. Yuanwu (圜悟) on the type: (大死底人)。(都無佛法道理玄妙得失是非長短) — the greatly-dead person has no Buddha's teaching, no stated principle, no mystery, no gain-and-loss, no right-and-wrong, no long-and-short; in the same Blue Cliff Record (碧巖錄) commentary he reports his teacher's wording — (五祖先師)。(謂之命根不斷)。(須是大死一番)。(却活始得) ('Wuzu, my late master, called it [having anything to lean on or any interpretation] the life-root not yet cut: one must die the great death once; only coming back to life will do'). Two idioms carry it. (1) (大死一番), 'die the great death once' (22 hits / 16 files): (直須絕名利)、(忘人我)，(大死一番方堪湊泊) ('you must cut off name-and-gain, forget self-and-other, and die the great death once — only then can you moor'; the recorded sayings of Chan Master Baiyu, 百愚禪師語錄), (秪管大死一番)，(不怕不活) ('just die the great death once — no fear you will not come back to life'; the recorded sayings of Chan Master Miyun, 密雲禪師語錄), and alongside it the stock verse (絕後再甦)。(欺君不得) ('revived after utter cutoff — he cannot be cheated'; 3 verbatim hits, 絕後再甦 alone 222 hits / 119 files, also written 絕後再蘇, 34 / 22). (2) (大死底人), 'the person who has died the great death' (99 hits / 58 files), which stands almost always inside the Zhaozhou–Touzi question — (大死底人) followed by (却)/(卻活時如何) ('when he comes back to life, what then?') in 74 of the 99 hits: (州問)。(大死底人)。(却活時如何) ('Zhou asked: the person who has died the great death — when he comes back to life, what then?') → Touzi answers (不許夜行)。(投明須到) ('no travelling by night; you must arrive by daylight'); the exact second clause (投明須到) recurs 192 times in 104 files. The compound (大死大活) ('greatly die, greatly live') is attested but rare (4 hits / 2 files). In Dahui's (大慧) letter (示東峯居士) ('shown to the layman Dongfeng') the phrase appears in a chain of appellations: (喚作默而常照)。(又喚作如大死底人)。(又喚作父母未生時事)。(又喚作空劫已前事) ('it is called "silent yet constantly shining"; also called "like a person who has died the great death"; also called "the matter before father and mother were born"; also called "the matter before the empty eon"'). One late imperial anthology's general preface gives a source-specific equivalence: 'this is called passing the heavy barrier; it is called one who greatly dies and greatly lives' (是則名為透重關，名為大死大活者). The explicit equation with 'passing the heavy barrier' (透重關) is a single late explanatory witness and remains provisional within the broader corpus-wide entry.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense; the (大死底人) ('person who has died the great death') case (Zhaozhou–Touzi) and the (大死一番) ('die the great death once') exhortation are two forms of the same term, and both are attested with revival wording alongside (却活時如何 'when he comes back to life, what then?' / 却活始得 'only coming back to life will do' / 不怕不活 'no fear you will not come back to life' / 絕後再甦 'revived after utter cutoff'). Multi-source across independent records (the 五燈會元 Compendium of the Five Lamps / the 碧巖錄 Blue Cliff Record / Dahui's recorded sayings 大慧語錄). Raw grep: (大死) 343 hits / 132 allowlist files (tag-stripped, 2026-07-11).

Occurrences.Kwic: 州問。大死底人。却活時如何。師曰。不許夜行。投明須到。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈會元. Zhaozhou Congshen is the exact questioner who asks how a person of great death is when revived; Touzi Datong gives the following answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大死底人。都無佛法道理玄妙得失是非長短。到這裏只恁麼休去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). In his commentary on the Zhaozhou–Touzi case, Yuanwu Keqin says the greatly dead person has no Buddhist principles, marvels, gain or loss, right or wrong, long or short, and simply rests there.

Occurrences.Kwic: 喚作默而常照。又喚作如大死底人。又喚作父母未生時事。又喚作空劫已前事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (大慧普覺禪師語錄), (示東峯居士); Dahui's own letter — (如大死底人) stands in his chain of appellations (喚作…又喚作…).

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲學斯道，必須大死一番始得。古德曰：「死盡偷心，方堪入室。絕後再甦，欺君不得。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 山西柏山楷禪師語錄. Baishan Dekai is the exact actor: his letter 與太谷眾居士 says 必須大死一番.

Occurrences.Kwic: 是則名為透重關，名為大死大活者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 御選語錄, imperial general preface. The Yongzheng Emperor is the exact author: in his three-barrier account he names penetrating the heavy barrier 'great death and great life.'
